period: Mars Year 30 (Ls 19 of MY30 to Ls 19 of MY31)

layers.name: Dust
layers.description: Dust in the atmosphere above each point: annual mean of the daily column dust optical depth (absorption at 9.3 um, total column down to the local surface) for Mars Year 30, a year without a global dust storm. Multiply by 2.6 for an approximate visible optical depth. 3-degree maps; it does not show dust lying on the ground or single storms.
layers.source: Montabone et al. (2015), Icarus 251, 65-95; LMD. CC BY-SA 3.0

layers.name: Temperature
layers.description: Annual mean temperature of the ground surface for Mars Year 30. A reanalysis: orbiter measurements of atmospheric temperature and dust are fed into a climate model, which computes the surface temperature. Day-night swings are large; the readout gives the coldest and warmest values. 5-degree grid, so it shows regions, not local sites.
layers.source: Holmes, Lewis & Patel (2020), Planet. Space Sci. 188, 104962. CC BY-NC-ND 4.0

layers.name: Wind
layers.description: Annual mean wind speed about 5 m above the ground (lowest model level) for Mars Year 30; arrows show the mean direction and are longer where the wind is steadier. A reanalysis: wind has never been measured globally on Mars, so it is computed by a climate model constrained by orbiter temperature and dust measurements. Gusts and local slope winds are not resolved on the 5-degree grid.
layers.source: Holmes, Lewis & Patel (2020), Planet. Space Sci. 188, 104962. CC BY-NC-ND 4.0

scalars.note: annual mean; OpenMARS reanalysis MY30, 5-degree grid, interpolated; not a direct measurement

scalars.label: Wind speed, mean
scalars.note: annual mean wind speed on the lowest model level (about 5 m above ground); OpenMARS reanalysis MY30, 5-degree grid, interpolated; not a direct measurement

scalars.label: Mean wind, eastward
scalars.note: annual mean eastward wind component on the lowest model level; OpenMARS reanalysis MY30

validation.check: Dust grid orientation: total/normalised optical depth follows surface pressure, i.e. MOLA elevation (r = -0.99; wrong orientations are far weaker)
Dust season: mean normalised optical depth is higher in Ls 180-360 (0.16) than in Ls 0-180 (0.08), the known dusty season
Dust annual mean within physical bounds (0.059 .. 0.257)
OpenMARS sampling covers the whole year: 2676 two-hourly steps on 223 sols (every 3rd sol, Ls 19 of MY30 to Ls 19 of MY31)
OpenMARS grid orientation: surface pressure follows MOLA elevation (r = -0.99; wrong orientations are far weaker)
Surface temperature is physically plausible: global mean 205 K, equator 217 K, poles 162 K
Surface temperature extremes within bounds (142 .. 312 K; CO2 frost point is about 145 K)
Mean near-surface wind speed within bounds (3.2 .. 18.3 m/s)
Download stayed within budget (0 MB of 500 MB)
